key_insight: Harrison.Rad 1.5 is a radiology-specific multimodal model designed to draft report text from images, prior studies, and clinical context, and it outperformed comparison systems on several radiology reporting and question-answering benchmarks.
clinical_relevance: If validated in practice, it could reduce radiologist reporting workload and help address imaging backlogs by speeding up structured report drafting and clinical interpretation support.
method: Three-stage training: radiology-report language adaptation, vision-encoder contrastive learning on ~6 million image-report pairs, and multi-turn visual-question-answering fine-tuning.
Uses interleaved text and visual inputs across plain-film radiology, including chest, musculoskeletal, abdominal, spine, pelvic x-rays, and mammography.
Evaluated with a Findings-Diagnosis framework plus public and internal benchmarks, including simulated FRCR 2B Short Case scoring.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, HR1.5 is reported to be the only evaluated system meeting the simulated FRCR passing standard and to achieve top results on closed-format clinical questions, internal multi-body-part and mammography reporting, and a primary chest reporting metric.
watch_item: Performance was assessed in benchmark and simulated settings, so real-world workflow integration, generalization across sites, and safety under clinical deployment still need careful prospective validation.
paper_title: Harrison.Rad 1.5 Technical Report: A radiology foundation model that can draft reports from images, priors and clinical context
